rationale.usefulness: The archived beta documentation supplies concrete agent prerequisites, a fixed-model command, usage accounting, headless behavior and surface-specific image generation. These support useful controlled coding and website trials in familiar tools. The report makes classroom and video-preparation applications explicitly proposed rather than tested, and savings and integration fidelity remain unmeasured, limiting broad actionability.
rationale.impact: This is a practical distribution and integration layer for existing hosted models and agent harnesses. The supplied evidence does not demonstrate a new model capability, task-equivalent economic improvement, adoption effects or an advance in AI methods. Its plausible significance is incremental workflow flexibility, below a demonstrated domain-level AI advance.
rationale.novelty: A common launcher spanning coding and desktop surfaces, optional cross-provider routing, and an included image skill provide some workflow differentiation. The primary evidence establishes packaging and access to existing capabilities rather than a new technical approach; the unresolved session-versus-request routing descriptions further limit claims about a distinctive router.
rationale.maturity: Detailed installation, configuration, billing and troubleshooting documentation makes a bounded trial feasible. Explicit beta status, changing model menus, conflicting Auto descriptions and the absence of installation or task tests constrain readiness to usable with material limits. No benchmark or reliability inference is needed to justify this middle score.
rationale.openness: Model selection and documentation give users some visibility and portability between hosted models. The execution path nevertheless depends on Together accounts and its hosted gateway, and optional Anthropic access has separate billing. The reviewed evidence does not establish the connector license, router implementation, every model license or reproducibility of the hosted service; open-model branding does not make the whole workflow open.

concerns: Non-blocking: the archived launch announcement and beta docs conflict about Auto routing frequency. The report prominently preserves this conflict and recommends pinned evaluation rather than treating either account as tested.

Non-blocking: savings, configuration guarantees and integration behavior are vendor documentation, not reproduced results. The report discloses this and does not claim universal license rights or local inference.

Optional practical detail: the same archived documentation says native web search is disabled in the ChatGPT Desktop Together Link profile. Naming that concrete limitation would strengthen the general warning that surface integrations can differ; the current report does not promise web-search parity.
